Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

whenever conjunction

also every time, as often as, each time

classical

Mart. 12.57.28: dormīre quotiēns libuit, īmus ad vīllam
Sen. Ep. 13.2: quī quotiēns cecidit contumācior resurrēxit

quotiēns

relative adverb, with the indicative; answered by totiēns

whenever, as often as

For a repeated action Latin puts the quotiēns-clause one step back in time: perfect beside a present (quotiēns libuit, īmus), pluperfect beside an imperfect.

Other words

  • cum (+ indicative) — whenever

    conjunction, with the indicative: perfect beside a present, pluperfect beside an imperfect · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 1.6.2: tum dēnique cum illō vēnimus; Cic. Verr. 2.5.27: cum ad aliquod oppidum vēnerat, eādem lectīcā ūsque ad cubiculum dēferēbātur (Lewis & Short)

    Cicero’s and Caesar’s usual way (Lewis & Short).

  • ubi — whenever, when

    conjunction, with the indicative · also used · classical · Ter. Eun. 813: Nōlunt ubi velīs; ubi nōlīs, cupiunt ultrō.

Examples

  • dormīre quotiēns libuit, īmus ad vīllam

    whenever we feel like sleeping, we go to the countryMart. 12.57.28

  • quī quotiēns cecidit contumācior resurrēxit

    who, every time he fell, got up again more stubbornSen. Ep. 13.2

  • nōs Tusculānō ita dēlectāmur ut nōbīsmet ipsīs tum dēnique cum illō vēnimus placeāmus

    I love Tusculum so much that I only like myself when I get thereCic. Att. 1.6.2

  • Nōlunt ubi velīs; ubi nōlīs, cupiunt ultrō.

    When you want them, they won’t; when you don’t, they’re keen of their own accord.Ter. Eun. 813

See also when, always, sometimes.
